# ORVIA — Agent build rules

**Product:** ORVIA Version 1 · **Build-pack edition:** 1.0 · **Prepared:** 19 September 2026  
**Authority:** [Approved master, document revision 1.4](sources/ORVIA_V1_Unified_Master_Rev_1_4_Vendor_Support_and_Data_Onboarding.md) · **Repository baseline:** `5a07649e5115995406e62de00b73e2c9fc560060`  
**Purpose:** Operating contract for all four development tracks; no application code is generated by this file.

This is an implementation specification, not evidence of completed software. `REQ` denotes a source-derived requirement, `OBS` a repository observation, `DESIGN` a proposed implementation detail, and `OPEN` a decision requiring its named owner. Exact technical shapes not supplied by the master are labelled design proposals; they do not silently become product or legal facts. Follow [Agent build rules](AGENT_BUILD_RULES.md).

## 1. Objective and protected material

Work in the existing verified `cyberfyx_orvia` repository. Preserve the separate `orvia-protype` presentation copy, its files and any shared runtime resources. Inspect real paths, Git state, linked directories, service ports, databases and volumes before any write/reset/build command. Never infer that separate directories imply separate persistence.

Do not edit, move, rename, format or append to idea/master documents. Hash the active master before and after a task that touches documentation or packaging. Do not alter sources to make an implementation look compliant. The attached revision 1.4 master controls V1; older 1.3/1.2 files are historical references.

No `git reset --hard`, blanket `git clean`, global container pruning, volume deletion, database truncation, force-push, history rewriting, real external messages or customer destructive action is authorised by these specifications. Obtain the relevant explicit operational authorisation. Preserve uncommitted/concurrent work and maintain a verified recovery path for unique content before deletion.

## 2. Non-negotiable V1 boundaries

Customer-local graph, policy, requests, identities, connectors, evidence, logs, imports, backups and frontend assets remain customer-local. Vendor stores contain only deliberately supplied business/licence/designated-contact information and individually approved fixed-schema diagnostics. No hashed/encrypted-data exception, runtime-directory sync or support impersonation.

No trained model, pretrained checkpoint, learned embeddings, model API, GPU, Lightning job, AI draft-import workaround or chat-history training in V1. Coding AI may use authorised source/docs and synthetic fixtures, never customer records, credentials or unrestricted incident logs. Direct customer support works without a helper.

Authenticated authority comes from the server, not a role in a request or hidden UI. Preserve tenant/legal-entity/environment/optional-subtenant scoping, MFA, TLS, validation, audit, idempotency, generation/epoch checks and exact approval bindings. Never return success after swallowing an error. Acknowledgement is not verification. A closed ticket is not a repaired privacy control.

## 3. Anti-bloat rule: every change must earn its place

Before adding a file, package, dependency, abstraction, endpoint or table, establish:

| Question | Required answer |
|---|---|
| Which approved requirement needs this? | A `FR-Mxx-nn`, `NFR-xx`, flow or source WP/section reference |
| Who consumes it now? | An existing/shipping execution path, test, build or explicitly required operations task |
| Is an equivalent implementation already present? | Search first; reuse the canonical owner or extend it |
| Is this the smallest coherent solution? | No parallel frameworks, speculative plugin systems or empty service shells |
| What establishes correctness? | A behaviour-oriented test and relevant failure/security case |
| Who owns it? | One package/module owner and reviewed import/public contract |

Do not generate empty folders for all 218 sections, one microservice per module, unused interfaces, trivial wrapper chains, one-line forwarding packages, speculative event buses, duplicate DTOs, mock production dashboards, temporary patch scripts, redundant README/status files or duplicate vendor/customer business logic. Shared code is justified by real reuse or an explicit security/test boundary, not hypothetical extensibility.

Do not minify or compress code to reduce line count. Clear naming, type safety, small explainable functions, useful rationale comments and robust errors are necessary code. Prefer deletion of proven redundancy over an arbitrary target number of files/lines. Tests, migrations, threat controls, recovery procedures and executable compatibility fixtures are not waste.

Use the existing dependency graph and lockfile. An addition needs a concrete capability, version/licence/security review and consumer. No framework/ORM/UI-library replacement solely for style. Do not hand-roll authentication or cryptography already provided by maintained reviewed libraries.

## 4. Production behaviour versus fixtures

Keep meaningful synthetic scenarios and failure injection in explicitly isolated test/evaluation paths. Remove hard-coded totals, fake effects, always-success responses, silent simulator fallback and production seed users. A simulator remains labelled synthetic; deleting its label does not make it real.

If a feature is unimplemented, fail explicitly and leave its status incomplete; do not fake success to pass a demo. Do not delete negative tests or acceptance criteria. Reference data, legal-source metadata and policy templates are not automatically dummy data; inspect their role and review state.

Do not delete imports/uploads/evidence/runtime files as source cleanup. Moving source must not rewrite applied migration names, checksum history, workflow identities or production schemas.

## 5. Contract and dependency discipline

Read the current executable schemas before edits. Extend the canonical schema/generator and update consumers together; never maintain a shadow OpenAPI/DTO/event enum by hand. Use deliberate public package exports. Browser code cannot import privileged backend/database/auth implementation through a shared barrel.

Domain state remains in a bounded owner module. Shared workflow infrastructure, consent, identity, evidence and database primitives must not be swallowed by `privacy-control`. Connector internals stay behind reviewed adapters, with no switch statement added to the domain for every vendor. Preserve database transaction boundaries when moving queries.

The master gives example physical layouts, not an instruction to produce duplicate `apps`, `frontend`, `services` and `modules` versions. Reconcile current paths with [TDD](TDD.md) and [transition](REPOSITORY_BASELINE_AND_TRANSITION.md) before moves; only one representation of each implementation survives.

## 6. One bounded change, one owner, one reviewer

Use the agreed four tracks: ChatGPT Work for requirements/contracts/integration review; Codex for backend/data/agents/platform tests; Claude Cowork for UX specifications/acceptance/runbooks and factual tracking; Claude Code for UI/API integration/browser tests. These are task roles, not claims of tool access or automatic cross-tool synchronisation.

Actual current repository instructions may assign paths differently. The human integration owner records explicit transfer before edits. One writer at a time for shared contracts, migrations, lockfile, root tooling and structural moves. Use separate worktrees/branches after verifying isolated runtime resources; do not let two agents independently change the same contract.

A task packet consists of: WP, requirement IDs, source sections, baseline commit, allowed files, dependencies, acceptance tests, chosen design/OPEN dependencies and forbidden side effects. Keep it in the existing task/handoff mechanism rather than a new document per substep.

## 7. Implementation loop and evidence

Inspect → select a small integrated requirement → define compatible contract/data changes → implement → run unit/integration/security/UI checks appropriate to the change → review → hand off exact evidence. A prototype pass is not a current pass after refactoring. Preserve failed runs and label test-environment failures separately from product failures.

Completion requires implemented backend and interface where applicable, persistent state, auth/scope checks, audit, documented API, failure paths, migrations/compatibility, local observability, tests and operational guidance. A feature is not complete because its page or endpoint exists.

Every result records exact commit/build, environment/profile, command, time, exit code, expected/observed behaviour and artifact location. Never substitute a plan, assertion that tests should pass, generated screenshot or obsolete report. No security/tenant/privacy gate is waived to satisfy delivery pressure. A test blocked by missing prerequisites remains blocked.

## 8. Decision handling

Do not invent payment/provider choices, licence grace periods, retention durations, legal applicability, GPU settings, supported hardware or current production readiness. The OPEN register names the responsible decision. Continue independent work; ask only for the essential unresolved choice or authorisation affecting the current action.

Routine implementation details within the approved boundary can use the labelled design proposals in this pack after contract review. Choices changing data destinations, destructive semantics, frameworks, public contracts or commercial promises require recorded owner approval. No new features unrelated to the approved V1 scope.

## 9. Finish with a useful handoff

State changed paths, implemented requirements, unchanged protected sources, actual tests/results, remaining limitations and the next dependency. Keep one factual state source; avoid generating another build plan, progress slide deck or duplicating this pack. Do not push, merge, deploy publicly, spend money or grant production permissions without the relevant authority.
